solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See one store kept by person very helpful mostly

indicators.note: being kept by something means sitting inside it, so the first pieces go within the other
mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: a brick is an informal word for a reliable, very helpful person
the Roman numeral one is I
a shop is a store

explanation.surface: Someone notices a shop being looked after by a very obliging person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look, but it is the definition: a bishop's see. 'mostly' cuts BRICK to BRIC, which holds I + SHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the diocese or office of a bishop, so the two words name the same church jurisdiction.

clue.text: People concealing diamonds in undergarments

indicators.note: concealing means holding something hidden inside

parts.note: bods is British slang for people or persons
ice is underworld slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: People have hidden diamonds in their underwear, smuggler-style.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodices are close-fitting women's upper garments, historically worn as undergarments beneath a dress.

clue.text: Weak person in trench

definitions.meaning: a gullible, feeble person, a fool
a covered trench dug towards an enemy position in siege warfare

explanation.surface: A feeble soldier cowers in a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a dupe or weakling, and a military siege trench dug by sappers.

clue.text: Boss always pursuing maidens maybe

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs, so maidens are an example of overs
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A boss forever chasing young women: a workplace predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maidens' suggests young women, but here they are cricket overs with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer supervises workers, so he is their boss or supervisor.

clue.text: Religious follower of sun-god, a good person at heart

indicators.note: at heart means placed in the middle of the other letters

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun-god
ST, short for saint, is a very good person

explanation.surface: A devotee of the sun-god is a good person deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is an adherent of Rastafarianism, a religion that arose in Jamaica.

clue.text: Old loony turning up in dress was dear, very much so

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: to comb hair is to dress it

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or loony

explanation.surface: A dotty old person's flamboyant outfit turned out to be very expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives STABO, read upwards in this down clue; 'dress' means groom hair, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To cost a bomb is a British idiom for being extremely expensive, matching very dear.

clue.text: Three goddesses, no good in competitions

indicators.note: no means the letter for good is left out

parts.note: the Three Graces of Greek myth are goddesses of charm and beauty

explanation.surface: Three goddesses fare badly in contests, like the judgment of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Races are speed contests, a common kind of competition.

clue.text: Broadcast in the auditorium put in place again

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the spoken sound of the word counts

parts.note: a broadcast programme is relayed, passed on by transmission

explanation.surface: A programme was transmitted in a hall and then put back in position.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaid is the past tense of relay in the sense of laying again, as with carpet or track.

clue.text: To survive as space traveller — hard and unpleasant

parts.note: a comet travels through space
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
rough can mean unpleasant, as in a rough time

explanation.surface: Getting through life as an astronaut is tough and nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: To come through a crisis is to get past it alive, an idiom for surviving.

clue.text: Horrible lice on underside of hospital plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on the underside of something means coming after it

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: horrible suggests the letters are a mess and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Nasty lice infest the bottom of a hospital, perhaps a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible' gives ICLE; in a down clue the lower piece comes later.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanicle is a woodland herb of the carrot family, once used in healing.

clue.text: Upset journalist turning away from colleagues en masse?

indicators.note: turning means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a stock journalist
the press is journalists collectively, the editor's colleagues as a body

explanation.surface: An editor, upset, turns away from the gathered press pack.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress someone is to sadden or dishearten them, which is to upset them.

clue.text: Athenian sage embracing second wise man

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: Solon was the lawgiver of ancient Athens, one of the Seven Sages
a mo, as in 'half a mo', is a second

explanation.surface: One ancient sage hugs another learned man.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon of the Bible is proverbial for wisdom, so the name stands for any wise man.

clue.text: Greek island occupied by one of its characters in a mask

indicators.note: occupied by means the island holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Cos, or Kos, is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a Greek character

explanation.surface: A Greek island is taken over by a masked local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people in a play, but here it means letters of the alphabet. 'mask' is a variant spelling of masque.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's Comus is a masque, a courtly verse drama with music, spelt mask in older usage.

clue.text: American flower girl is very good, imbibing only a small drink

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the drink goes inside

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl
pi, short for pious, means very good
a sip is just a little drink

explanation.surface: A well-behaved American girl only drinks a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river, something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mississippi is the great river of the USA, and a river is a crossword flower because it flows.

clue.text: Destroyer coming back into room, showing more primitive characteristics

indicators.note: into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: an attic is a room under the roof

indicators.note: coming back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Siva, or Shiva, is the Hindu god known as the Destroyer

explanation.surface: A warship reverses into a room, behaving like a throwback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' suggests a warship but is the Hindu god; 'coming back' gives AVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavistic describes a reversion to traits of remote ancestors, a return to primitive ways.

clue.text: Son set out travelling, being sustained

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A son leaves home on a long journey, kept going by support.
explanation.definitionFit: Sostenuto is the musical direction meaning sustained, played with notes held.

clue.text: Yet to be paid, and restless

definitions.meaning: an account not yet settled is outstanding, still owed
disturbed and agitated, unable to settle down

explanation.surface: Someone with unpaid bills feels uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word covers an outstanding debt and a state of agitation.

clue.text: Genuine agreement for peace, about to be discarded

indicators.note: to be discarded means this letter is thrown out

parts.note: a truce is an agreement to stop fighting
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A real ceasefire, about to be scrapped, as such deals often are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be discarded' reads as a phrase but splits: 'about' is C, 'to be discarded' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and true are synonyms, both meaning real or authentic.

clue.text: A knight in traditional order breaking ranks?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: trad is short for traditional
N is the chess notation for a knight
the OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A knight in a time-honoured order of chivalry falls out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: ranks broken up end in no particular order.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking ranks, soldiers scatter haphazardly, with no plan or order, which is at random.

clue.text: A drink goes round for a win

indicators.note: goes round means encircling the other piece

parts.note: gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A round of drinks is bought to celebrate a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A gain is something won or acquired, a profit or advantage, so it is a win.

clue.text: Looked quickly in church — organ observed going round

indicators.note: the organ is seen to go round the church letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a gland is an organ of the body
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone peered quickly round a church while the organ was heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' in a church suggests the musical instrument, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to look briefly, so glanced means looked quickly.

clue.text: Wreckers after setback regret being heavily shod?

indicators.note: the regret is being heavily shod, that is placed inside the clogs

parts.note: sabots are heavy wooden clogs, so wearing them is being heavily shod

indicators.note: set back means the letters are put in reverse order

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Vandals strike after a setback, stamping about in heavy boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' gives EUR. Sabotage is traditionally said to come from wooden clogs thrown into machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Saboteurs deliberately destroy or damage things, so they are wreckers.

clue.text: Boy needs practice session to produce poetry

parts.note: a son is a boy
in cricket the nets are a batting practice session

explanation.surface: A lad needs training to write verse.
explanation.walkthrough: NETS is cricket practice, batting in netted lanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonnets are fourteen-line poems, so collectively they are poetry; a plural for a mass noun.

clue.text: Shame about basic accommodation for one who can't get out

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece

parts.note: a sin is a shameful act
a hut is a simple, basic dwelling

explanation.surface: It is a disgrace how basic the housing is for someone housebound.
explanation.definitionFit: A shut-in is an invalid confined to the home, unable to leave.

clue.text: I hate sect struggling to be stylish?

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters writhe about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who hates a cult tries to look fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetic relates to beauty and taste, so a stylish thing may be called aesthetic; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Money reportedly in secret store

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the clue word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Money is said to be in a hidden stash.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden stockpile of goods or weapons, a secret store.

clue.text: Poisonous element getting female sickly-looking

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic, a poison
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A woman given arsenic would soon look pale and ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey and pale as ash, the colour of someone ill.

clue.text: What may be invested in Edinburgh?

definitions.text: What may be invested in Edinburgh?

parts.words: What may be invested in Edinburgh?
parts.note: the clue hints at money put into a Scottish venture, while Edinburgh is also the chief city of Scotland

explanation.surface: A question about investments in the Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is money invested in Edinburgh; the other is the status Edinburgh holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both money invested and a seat of government, and Edinburgh is Scotland's seat.

clue.text: Once I'd messed with one drug and another

indicators.note: messed with means tampered with, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is slang for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A former user confesses to dabbling with various drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed with' rearranges ONCE ID into CODEIN; E is added; 'another' defines it as a second drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate painkiller, so it is another drug besides ecstasy.

clue.text: President to have regard for, leader no more

indicators.note: leader no more means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to like someone is to have regard for them

explanation.surface: A president to be respected, no longer in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ike was the nickname of Dwight D. Eisenhower, US President in the 1950s.

clue.text: Pub wants leading party host to engender spirit

indicators.note: leading means coming in front of the other piece

parts.note: a DJ hosts the music at a party
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub needs a lead DJ to get the party atmosphere going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests party mood or a drink, but means a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A djinn is a genie, a spirit of Arabian and Islamic lore.

clue.text: Leaders seem heartless, sadly lacking vision

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
heartless means the middle letters are removed

explanation.surface: A complaint that our leaders seem callous and short of vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves SM from 'seem'; 'sadly' rearranges LEADERS + SM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamless sleep has no dreams, and dreams are visions seen in sleep.
